WMB.thesis_one_line: The pipeline company moving a third of America's natural gas is growing steadily, but its share price already assumes years of faster growth than we expect.
kill_criteria: Company-reported Debt-to-Adjusted EBITDA above 4.25x at any quarter end (30 Jun 2026: 3.67x; 2026 guide midpoint about 3.75x pro forma for Momentum).
2026 Adjusted EBITDA guidance low end below $8.3bn at any release (current "$8.3 billion to $8.5 billion", acc. 0000107263-26-000024).
2026 growth capex guidance raised above $7.9bn without an offsetting increase in the EBITDA range (current $7.3 billion to $7.9 billion).
Year-over-year Adjusted EBITDA growth below 3% for two consecutive quarters (Q2 2026: +6.2%).
AFFO dividend coverage below 1.8x for a quarter (Q2 2026: 2.26x).
key_adverse_facts: TTM free cash flow about -$108m: operating cash flow $5,994m vs cash capex $6,102m; 2026 growth capex guide raised from $6.1-6.7bn to $7.3-7.9bn in six months
Net debt about $30.6bn consolidated (3.76x TTM Adj. EBITDA, company-reported 3.67x); $2.2bn of debt due within one year; dependent on capital markets and JV funding
Momentum Midstream acquisition (up to $5.5bn, about $2bn in stock, 8.5x 2027 EBITDA) not yet closed as of 2026-09-25; 2026 EBITDA raise is acquisition-linked and organic raise not disclosed
Q2 2026 GAAP EPS $0.68 vs Adjusted $0.50: includes $126m gain on Brazos Permian II sale and $106m derivative swing
Valuation 30.5x TTM Adjusted EPS, 13.4x trailing AFFO; insiders sold 12 times and bought never since 2026-03-25
data_conflicts: Triage said leverage 4.3x and 'essentially flat forward growth'; filings show 3.67x company-reported (3.76x my calc) and 2026 Adjusted EBITDA guide midpoint +8.4% vs 2025's $7,750m
b1 composite is about the 2nd percentile (FCF/price -0.13%, negative) because growth capex exceeds operating cash flow; not a sign of weak earnings
WMB.confidence_in_thesis: medium: asset quality and guidance record are high-confidence; the verdict rests on my reverse-DCF and ke assumptions (8.5% base, 7.5-9.5% range) and on no peer multiples being computed

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No V1 row exists for WMB. Reverse DCF: $69.26 needs about 10.3% a year dividend growth (about 7.1% AFFO/share growth) for ten years at 8.5% cost of equity vs my base of about 5%.

WMB.scenario_basis: 2026E Adj. EPS $2.35 (1H actual $1.23 + my 2H est.), 2029 Adj. EPS $2.55/$3.00/$3.45, exit P/E 20x/24x/27x, dividends about $6.6 over 3y ($2.10 growing about 5%); start $69.26

BA.thesis_one_line: Boeing is recovering as factories speed up and cash flow turns positive, but the share price already assumes it reaches its $10 billion cash target by about 2029.
kill_criteria: 2026 free cash flow outlook cut below the "$1 billion to $3 billion" range, or withdrawn, at any earnings call.
737 production rate cut below 42 a month, or any new FAA production cap or halt (current: transitioning from 42 to 47 a month per 10-Q).
737-7 or 737-10 certification not achieved by 31 Dec 2026, or 777-9 first delivery guided later than 2027 (both currently "2026" and "2027").
Consolidated debt above $50bn at any quarter end, or a downgrade to sub-investment grade at S&P or Moody's (30 Jun 2026: $45.9bn; BBB- and Baa3).
2026 737 deliveries tracking below 450 (target "500 airplanes this year"; Q2 2026 delivered 129, 1H26 total 314 across all programs).
key_adverse_facts: TTM free cash flow about -$0.2bn; 2026 outlook only $1-3bn, back-end loaded (1H26 FCF -$823m); $700m DOJ payment in Q3 2026
Q2 2026 GAAP loss per share $(0.67), core $(0.76); $280m VC-25B charge in Q2 2026; $4.9bn 777X charge in Q3 2025
Consolidated debt $45.9bn vs cash and investments $20.0bn; BBB-/Baa3 investment grade at the floor; tangible equity about -$13.0bn
Securities class action partially certified 16 Mar 2026 (appeal pending); 737-9 door-plug investigations and suits pending; no loss range estimable
No numeric guidance in releases; FCF outlook and $10bn target come from call transcripts only
data_conflicts: b1 ROE 0.40 (80th pct) is an artefact of $6.1bn equity and the $11.83 per share one-off Q4 2025 divestiture gain; GAAP TTM EPS $2.31 is not a run rate
Triage said FAA production-rate caps: 10-Q now says 737 is moving from 42 to 47 a month with FAA concurrence; negative tangible equity is confirmed (total equity is +$6.1bn)
BA.confidence_in_thesis: medium: operating recovery well evidenced; the verdict depends on my 2029 FCF base ($8.5bn vs the $10bn management calls very attainable) and a 9% cost of equity

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No V1 row exists for BA. Reverse DCF: $198.07 needs about $10.4bn of 2029 free cash flow at 9% cost of equity vs my base $8.5bn (worth about $162 per share). [Corrected 2026-10-08 (DV05): The 9% cost of equity had no stated risk-free rate or ERP. At CAPM 10.6% (rf 5.17%, beta ~1.21, ERP 4.5%) the price needs ~$13.7bn of 2029 FCF (not $10.4bn) and the $8.5bn base is worth ~$125 per share (not ~$162); re-entry trigger ~$125. Scenario returns unchanged. implied_vs_base above strengthened.]

BA.scenario_basis: 2029 FCF $5.0bn/$8.5bn/$11.0bn, 830m diluted shares (incl. mandatory convertible), exit 21x FCF (4.75% yield), no dividend; start $198.07

MOS.thesis_one_line: A fertilizer maker losing money as a key raw material, sulfur, gets expensive; steady potash and a refinanced balance sheet help, but cash flow is negative.
kill_criteria: Phosphate segment adjusted EBITDA below zero in any quarter (Q2 2026: $128m; my estimate for Q4 2026 roughly $30-50m).

Consolidated net debt / TTM adjusted EBITDA above 3.5x at a quarter end, or the credit facility interest-coverage ratio below 3.0x (30 Jun 2026: about 2.6x on TTM adjusted EBITDA; covenant maximum debt to capitalisation 0.65).
Realised mine-gate MOP price below $250 per tonne for two consecutive quarters (Q2 2026: $275; Q3 guide "$270 - $290").
Trailing-twelve-month free cash flow still below zero at 30 Jun 2027 (30 Jun 2026: about -$948m).
Any further single-quarter notable items above $300m (Q1 2026: $323m; Q2 2026: $351m).
key_adverse_facts: TTM free cash flow about -$948m; dividend (about $280m a year) not covered; GAAP net loss in each of the last three quarters (-$519m, -$258m, -$273m)
Sulfur contract $705 per long ton reaches Q4 2026 results vs $522 average in Q2; Phosphate gross margin $(4) per tonne in Q2; Fertilizantes Q3 EBITDA guided below Q2
Phosphate production guidance withdrawn (Q1); Faustina idled, Bartow at 40% rate; Araxa and Patrocinio idled with $442m of Q1 charges
Asset retirement obligations $2.5bn (gypstack closure) and New Wales stack repairs
Net debt about $5.56bn: 2.6x TTM adjusted EBITDA but about 3.4x on Q2 annualised and about 4.6x on my Q4 run-rate estimate
data_conflicts: Triage net debt/EBITDA 3.4x matches Q2 annualised EBITDA ($1,628m); on TTM adjusted EBITDA ($2,134m) it is about 2.6x
Triage sulfur 'about $1,200 per ton' was a spot peak cited in the Q1 release; the Q3 contract settled at $705 per long ton (Q2 release)
MOS.confidence_in_thesis: low-to-medium: potash and liquidity are well evidenced; phosphate recovery timing depends on sulfur normalising, which management itself says has uncertain timing

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No V1 row exists for MOS. Reverse DCF: operating equity of $5.56bn (ex Ma'aden) needs about $0.46bn of 2029 free cash flow at 10% cost of equity vs my base $0.40bn.

MOS.scenario_basis: 2029 adj. EBITDA $1.5bn/$2.3bn/$3.2bn, exit EV/EBITDA 5.5x/5.5x/6.5x, Ma'aden stake $1.4bn/$1.75bn/$2.0bn, net debt $6.8bn/$6.0bn/$5.0bn, ARO net $1.5bn, 318m shares, dividends $1.76/$2.64/$2.64; start $23.01
